_about: Two end-to-end runs on the invented document sets in examples/. Each prompt supplies every answer the skill would otherwise ask for, so a run needs no interaction. The runs are graded on provenance (every date and figure in the complaint is in the documents), on the state procedure being verified with sources, and on the pleading rules. The baseline is the same prompt with no skill.

evals.name: river-oak-pro-se-california
evals.prompt:
I'm Dana Rivera, Jordan's mother. Please draft our due process complaint from the school documents in the documents/ folder of this case folder. We're in California and I'm filing it myself, without a lawyer; I plan to file on April 17, 2026. My phone, email and our address are in the IEP.

Please don't stop to ask me questions — everything you need is below. If something is genuinely missing, leave it blank and tell me at the end rather than guessing. You may confirm on my behalf every reading that checks out against the page; I'll go through the sources afterwards.

The claims I want to bring: (1) the IEP is inadequate — the reading goal was carried over unchanged from the year before and they refused to revise it; (2) they didn't implement the reading services in the IEP; (3) they didn't evaluate Jordan after I asked for a reevaluation in writing.

What I'm asking for: an IEP meeting within 15 days to adopt measurable reading goals based on current assessment data; an independent educational evaluation in reading and written expression at the district's expense; compensatory specialized academic instruction equal to the minutes not delivered from October 6, 2025 through February 27, 2026; and the IEP implemented as written, with quarterly service logs sent to me.

What happened, in my words: The IEP team kept the same reading fluency goal on September 8, 2025 that it had set on March 11, 2024, and refused on March 12, 2026 to change it even though Jordan's fluency was 21, 24 and 23 words per minute on the three progress reports. The district stopped the small-group reading block on October 6, 2025 and delivered about 95 minutes a week of the 240 minutes the IEP requires through February 27, 2026. I asked in writing on December 2, 2025 for a reevaluation of Jordan's reading and have not received an assessment plan.

How I learned of it: from the progress reports dated November 14, 2025, January 23, 2026 and March 6, 2026; from the service delivery log the district gave me for September 8, 2025 to February 27, 2026; from the prior written notice dated March 12, 2026; and from Mr. Ellison's email of December 4, 2025.

Effect on Jordan: he read 22 words per minute in August 2025 and 23 words per minute in March 2026. The IEP says the end-of-second-grade benchmark is 87 words per minute. He is in third grade.

Please put the finished complaint, and anything that shows me where each fact came from, in this case folder.
evals.expected_output: complaint.md/complaint.html captioned before the California Office of Administrative Hearings, pro se signature block, three lettered sections whose every date and figure appears in the five PDFs, sources.md tracing each paragraph to document and page, verification-report.md saying FINAL, and state.json citing official California pages with URLs and access dates.
expectations: A finished complaint file exists in the case folder (complaint.md or an equivalent single document).
The caption names the Office of Administrative Hearings (California), not the California Department of Education, as the body the complaint is before.
The complaint contains the student's name, the residence address including the ZIP code 95833, and the school name Willow Creek Elementary School.
Every calendar date written in the statement of the problems appears in the text of the five PDFs.
Every number written in the statement of the problems appears in the text of the five PDFs (no arithmetic the documents do not state, such as a computed shortfall).
The statement of the problems is in the third person: no 'I', 'my', 'me' or 'we' outside a quotation.
The statement of the problems does not call the student by his given name (Jordan); it says Student.
The statement of the problems contains no regulation citations and no legal conclusions ('violated', 'denied FAPE', 'in violation of').
The complaint contains no outcome language ('likely to prevail', 'strong case', 'a hearing officer would').
A proposed resolution section lists the four remedies the parent asked for.
A sources file traces each factual paragraph of the statement to a document and a page number.
The state's filing procedure (where the original goes, the copy to the district, the filing address, the two-year window) is recorded with URLs of official California pages and an access date.
A verification report exists and reports the status FINAL with zero blocking findings.
The run did not ask the user any question before finishing.

evals.name: pine-hollow-counsel-north-carolina
evals.prompt:
Draft a due process complaint from the documents in the documents/ folder of this case folder. I represent the parent.

Counsel: Renée Castillo, North Carolina State Bar No. 61042, Castillo Education Law PLLC, 1200 Example Avenue, Suite 4, Raleigh, NC 27601, (555) 010-6104, rcastillo@example.com. Client: Grace Okafor, parent of Maya Okafor. Filing in North Carolina; planned filing date June 1, 2026. The student's and parent's details are in the IEP.

Do not stop to ask me questions; what you need is here. If something is genuinely missing, leave it blank and say so at the end. Confirm on my behalf every reading that is verified against its page; I will review the sources.

Claims: failure to implement the IEP (the speech-language therapy), and failure to evaluate appropriately, including the refusal to fund the independent educational evaluation the parent requested.

Relief: compensatory speech-language therapy, delivered individually, equal to the minutes not delivered from September 22, 2025 to the date of the order; an independent educational evaluation in speech-language and written expression at public expense; and restoration of individual speech-language therapy at 60 minutes per week as the IEP requires.

Facts. What the district did or failed to do: the IEP of August 21, 2025 requires 60 minutes per week of individual speech-language therapy; from the week of September 22, 2025 the district delivered 30 minutes per week in a group of three, with no service in three weeks, for a total of 690 minutes against 1,320 required through January 30, 2026, and did not amend the IEP; the parent requested an independent educational evaluation in writing on November 10, 2025 and the district refused it on December 4, 2025 without filing for a hearing; the district's May 6, 2025 evaluation did not assess written expression. How the client learned of it: from the service log the district sent on January 21, 2026, from the prior written notice of December 4, 2025, and from the student's own reports. Effect on the student: her expressive language remains at the 2nd percentile per the May 2025 CELF-5 and she has become reluctant to speak in class, per the IEP's present levels. Relief sought: as above.

Put the complaint, the sources and the verification report in this case folder.
evals.expected_output: complaint.md captioned for the North Carolina Office of Administrative Hearings with the represented signature block (firm, bar number), two lettered sections whose every date and figure appears in the four PDFs, sources.md, a state block citing official North Carolina sources including the one-year window in N.C. Gen. Stat. § 115C-109.6(b) and the OAH petition procedure, and a verification report that warns that the May 6, 2025 evaluation is outside the one-year window without deciding the point.
expectations: A finished complaint file exists in the case folder.
The caption names the North Carolina Office of Administrative Hearings as the body the complaint is before.
The signature block carries counsel's name, the firm, and the bar number 61042, and does not say pro se or self-represented.
The complaint contains the student's name, the residence address including the ZIP code 27999, and the school name Cedar Ridge Middle School.
Every calendar date written in the statement of the problems appears in the text of the four PDFs.
Every number written in the statement of the problems appears in the text of the four PDFs.
The statement of the problems is in the third person and does not call the student by her given name (Maya).
The statement of the problems contains no regulation citations and no legal conclusions.
The complaint contains no outcome language.
The state's limitations window is recorded as one year (12 months), sourced to N.C. Gen. Stat. § 115C-109.6(b) or an official North Carolina page quoting it, not assumed to be two years.

The state's filing procedure names the OAH petition form (Form H-06E) or the OAH filing address 1711 New Hope Church Road, Raleigh, with an official URL and an access date, and the certificate of service names the district's superintendent.
The run flags, as a warning and not a decision, that the May 6, 2025 evaluation event falls outside the one-year window measured from the June 1, 2026 filing date.
A sources file traces each factual paragraph of the statement to a document and a page number.
The run did not ask the user any question before finishing.
